title: Diwali Shopping in Delhi 2026: Which Market Sells What
summary: A product-to-market guide for Diwali shopping in Delhi. Decorations, festive clothes, sweets, gifts, puja items and lighting mapped by market.
body_markdown:
Delhi has more than a dozen markets that stock Diwali items, but each one carries a completely different product range. Sadar Bazaar handles wholesale decorations. Chandni Chowk handles festive clothes and sweets. Bhagirath Palace handles LED lights and electrical decorations. Khan Market handles premium gift hampers. Walking into the wrong market for a specific product wastes an entire afternoon.


This guide is organised by what you want to buy, not by market name. Find the product, find the market, and plan the trip.


Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8. Dhanteras is Friday, November 6. The shopping window starts roughly two weeks before and peaks in the final four days.


## **Decorations, Diyas and Rangoli Materials**


Most of Delhi’s Diwali decoration stock originates from one market. Understanding the supply chain explains why prices vary so much across the city.


### **Sadar Bazaar: The Wholesale Source**


Sadar Bazaar is where neighbourhood shops, event planners and housing society committees buy their Diwali decorations. The lanes near Swadeshi Market carry the highest density of festival stalls during the Diwali season.


What you can buy here:


- Earthen diyas from roughly Rs 1 per piece in bulk
- Decorative painted diyas from Rs 5 to Rs 20 each
- Torans and bandhanwar (door hangings)
- Artificial marigold garlands and flower strings
- Rangoli stencils and powder colours
- Paper lanterns, wall hangings and decorative candles
- Lakshmi Ganesh idol sets in clay, brass and silver-plated finishes


The pricing is wholesale-first. Even single-item purchases are significantly cheaper than retail, but buying in quantity drops the per-piece cost further.


### **Dilli Haat INA: Artisan and Handmade Options**


For decorations that carry craft identity rather than factory uniformity, Dilli Haat stocks handmade terracotta diyas from Rajasthani and UP artisans, hand-painted candle holders, and embroidered torans. Prices are higher than Sadar Bazaar but the design quality is in a different category.


## **LED Lights, Fairy Lights and Electrical Decorations**


### **Bhagirath Palace: Wholesale Lighting at Source Pricing**


Bhagirath Palace in the Chandni Chowk area is the wholesale electrical market that supplies lighting retailers across North India. During Diwali, the stock includes:


- LED string lights and rice lights
- Fairy light curtains and net lights
- Decorative bulbs and neon signage
- Festival illumination sets for balconies, terraces and shopfronts


A string of 100 LED lights that retails for Rs 200 to Rs 300 in a neighbourhood store is available here for Rs 80 to Rs 120. The savings on a full home or shopfront decoration are substantial.


Bhagirath Palace sits adjacent to the Sadar Bazaar area, so a combined visit covering both decorations and lighting is practical in a single trip. Carry cash, as most wholesale shops here prefer it.


## **Festive Clothes and Ethnic Wear**


The festive clothing market in Delhi is split by budget and geography. Different markets serve different price ranges.


### **Chandni Chowk: Widest Range, Every Budget**


Nai Sarak in Chandni Chowk carries the broadest range of festive ethnic wear in Delhi. Women’s suits, sarees, kurta sets and lehenga-style festive outfits are available from Rs 500 for basic kurtas up to Rs 50,000+ for heavy embroidered pieces. The[Chandni Chowk market guide](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/chandni-chowk-market-timings-shopping-guide/) covers the full lane-by-lane breakdown.


### **Lajpat Nagar Central Market: Mid-Range South Delhi**


Lajpat Nagar carries ethnic wear, festive kurtas, designer replicas and matching accessories at prices roughly 20 to 30 percent below mall retail. The[Lajpat Nagar market guide](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/lajpat-nagar-market-timings-shopping-guide/) has the full details.


### **Sarojini Nagar: Budget Festive Wear**


Sarojini handles the budget end. Festive kurtas, ethnic tops and budget suits in the Rs 200 to Rs 1,000 range. The trade-off is quality variability and extremely heavy Diwali-week crowds.


## **Sweets and Dry Fruit Gift Boxes**


Diwali gifting in Delhi runs heavily on mithai and dry fruits. The market you choose depends on whether you want wholesale pricing or branded packaging.


### **Chandni Chowk Halwai Lane: Traditional Sweets**


The halwai shops between Dariba Kalan and the Fatehpuri end of Chandni Chowk have been selling Diwali sweets for generations. The stock covers motichoor laddu, kaju katli, barfi, petha and son papdi, with gift packaging from simple boxes at Rs 200 to premium decorated thalis at Rs 2,000.


### **Chawri Bazaar: Wholesale Dry Fruits**


For dry fruit gift boxes in quantity, Chawri Bazaar carries almonds, cashews, pistachios, walnuts and figs at wholesale pricing. Pre-packed gift sets start from Rs 300 for a 500-gram box. Custom branded boxes for corporate gifting are available at the larger shops.


### **Bengali Market: Branded Sweet Shops**


Bengali Market near Connaught Place carries the branded options: Nathu’s, Bengali Sweet House and similar establishments with standardised quality and packaging.


## **Puja Items for Lakshmi Puja**


The Lakshmi Puja on Diwali night requires a specific set of items that most households do not stock year-round.


### **Sadar Bazaar: One-Stop for Most Items**


Sadar Bazaar covers the majority of puja requirements in a single trip:


- Lakshmi Ganesh idols (clay from Rs 20, brass from Rs 500)
- Puja thalis (steel from Rs 50, brass from Rs 200)
- Kalash (brass from Rs 100)
- Diyas and cotton wicks
- Dhoop, agarbatti and camphor


### **Temple-Adjacent Stalls: Pre-Assembled Kits**


For convenience, the stalls outside Hanuman Mandir at Connaught Place and similar temple vendors sell pre-assembled puja samagri packets containing sindoor, akshat, haldi, chandan, mauli, supari and cotton at Rs 50 to Rs 150 per kit.


## **Premium Gifts and Corporate Hampers**


### **Khan Market: Curated Gift Shopping**


Khan Market carries the premium end of Diwali gifting. Imported chocolates, gourmet teas, designer candles, home fragrance sets and curated gift boxes. Prices start at Rs 1,500 and go well above Rs 10,000. Custom branding for corporate orders is standard at the established shops.


### **Dilli Haat: Artisan Gifts**


Handcrafted items from artisans across India. Pottery, textile pieces, leather goods, wooden artefacts and hand-painted items in the Rs 200 to Rs 3,000 range. These make distinctive gifts that carry regional identity.


## **Utensils and Metal Items for Dhanteras**


Buying metal on Dhanteras (November 6) is considered auspicious, and the demand peaks sharply on this single day.


### **Narain Market, Sadar Bazaar**


Steel utensils, pressure cookers, non-stick cookware, ceramic dinner sets and brass items at prices typically 15 to 25 percent below MRP on branded items. Narain Market on Dhanteras day sees queues extending into the lanes. Arrive early.


### **Karol Bagh**


Branded kitchenware and home appliance stores for buyers who want receipts, warranties and a retail shopping experience. The[Karol Bagh market guide](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/karol-bagh-market-timings-shopping-guide/) covers the full range.


## **Planning Your Shopping Route**


A practical two-trip plan covers most Diwali shopping needs.


- **Trip 1 (half day, weekday morning):** Sadar Bazaar plus Bhagirath Palace. This covers decorations, diyas, puja items and lighting in one visit. Allow 3 to 4 hours.
- **Trip 2 (half day, separate day):** Chandni Chowk or Lajpat Nagar. This covers festive clothes, sweets, dry fruits and gift items.


For premium gifts, Khan Market or Dilli Haat works as a third, shorter visit.


## **When to Shop**


The widest selection and best prices are available 10 to 14 days before Diwali. By the final three days, popular items at wholesale shops sell out, and remaining stock carries firmer pricing with less room for negotiation.


Weekday mornings between 10 AM and 12 PM offer the least crowded experience at every market. Saturday afternoons during Diwali fortnight are the worst time to visit any Delhi market.


***Note:*** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Which is the best market for diwali shopping in delhi?**


It depends on the product. Sadar Bazaar for decorations, Chandni Chowk for clothes and sweets, Bhagirath Palace for lighting, and Khan Market for gifts.


### **Where can I buy wholesale Diwali decorations in Delhi?**


Sadar Bazaar is the largest wholesale market for decorations, offering diyas, torans, rangoli materials and garlands at bulk rates.


### **Which market has the cheapest Diwali lights in Delhi?**


Bhagirath Palace in Chandni Chowk is the wholesale electrical market with LED lights and fairy lights at the lowest prices in the city.


### **Where should I buy Diwali sweets in Delhi?**


The halwai lane in Chandni Chowk for traditional sweets. Bengali Market for branded sweet shops. Chawri Bazaar for wholesale dry fruit gift boxes.


### **When should I start Diwali shopping in Delhi?**


Start 10 to 14 days before Diwali for the best selection. The final 3 days see sellouts at wholesale shops and firmer pricing.


### **Is Sarojini Nagar good for Diwali clothes?**


Sarojini carries budget festive kurtas and ethnic wear at Rs 200 to Rs 1,000. Quality varies, and Diwali-week crowds are heavy.


### **Where can I buy Dhanteras utensils in Delhi?**


Narain Market in Sadar Bazaar for wholesale steel and brass. Karol Bagh for branded kitchenware with warranties. Arrive early on Dhanteras.


### **Which market has the best Diwali gift hampers in Delhi?**


Khan Market for premium and corporate hampers. Dilli Haat for artisan handcrafted gifts at mid-range prices.


### **Can I cover Sadar Bazaar and Bhagirath Palace in one trip?**


The two markets are adjacent and a combined visit covers decorations, diyas, puja items and lighting in a single 3 to 4 hour morning trip.


### **What are the timings for Delhi markets during Diwali?**


Most markets extend hours during Diwali week. Some shops open on their regular weekly off. Check individual market guides for current timings.
